extracted.intended_audience: applicants and institutional officials preparing or administering NIH Career Development (K) Award applications (including mentors and grants management staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and application/review criteria for NIH Career Development (K) Awards, covering eligibility, appointment and effort requirements, institutional commitment, application components, responsible conduct of research training, prior support rules, and special provisions (e.g., K99→R00 transition, concurrent support).

rubrics_metrics.name: K99→R00 transition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient is required to secure a tenure track, full-time assistant professor position or equivalent in order to transition to the R00 independent phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition to the R00 phase is not guaranteed; the transition application is administratively reviewed by NIH staff (not peer-reviewed). There should not be any delay between the K99 phase and the R00 phase. R00 award recipients are expected to compete successfully for independent R01 support from NIH during the R00 phase. See New Investigators Program web page and specific NOFO for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual non-mentored CDA eligibility (doctoral + independent support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent (non-mentored) CDAs (e.g., K02, K05, K07 leadership, K24) require candidates to have a doctoral degree and independent, peer-reviewed support at the time the award is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some participating NIH ICs require the candidate to have an NIH research grant from their IC at time of application; other ICs will accept peer-reviewed support from other sources. Planning, direction, and execution of the proposed program and research are the responsibility of the applicant and sponsoring institution. Independent CDAs are not transferable and may sometimes be renewable. Some independent CDAs also require the candidate to serve as research mentors for junior researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional scientist development program constraints (K12/KL2)
rubrics_metrics.description: K12 and KL2 awards provide support to an institution to develop independent basic or clinical scientists (scholars) selected by the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specified number of scholar positions are awarded in a K12; K12 is solicited only by IC-specific NOFOs. K12 is subject to NIH Standard Terms of Award; carryover of unobligated balances generally requires prior written approval. K12 awards are generally not transferable to another institution. KL2 is used when institutional mentored programs are part of a Clinical and Translational Science Award Consortium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Research Curriculum Award (K30) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: K30 is awarded to an institution to stimulate inclusion of high-quality, multidisciplinary, didactic training as part of career development for clinical investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports development or improvement of core courses providing in-depth instruction in fundamental skills, methodologies, and theories necessary for the well-trained, independent clinical researcher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for CDAs may be submitted on behalf of the candidate by any domestic for-profit or non-profit public or private institution/organization (e.g., universities, colleges, hospitals, laboratories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign organizations are not eligible to apply for CDAs, but foreign components may apply. Check specific NOFO for any IC-specific limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the candidate (PD/PI) may develop an application for a CDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Multiple PD/PI applications are not accepted for individual CDAs; institutional CDAs should check the NOFO for allowability of Multiple PD/PIs. For mentored CDA programs, candidates who are well-established in their fields are considered ineligible unless they provide justification that they are not already established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of being 'well-established' (mentored CDA ineligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some indications of having achieved 'well-established' status include tenure or the equivalent, a substantial publication record, or considerable research support that already requires commitment of a major part of the candidate's time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who meet one or more of these criteria must provide justification in the application that they are not already established in their field if applying for mentored CDAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are generally required to hold a research or health-professional doctoral degree or its equivalent; eligibility for some CDAs is limited to applicants with health professional doctoral degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific degree requirements are outlined in the NOFO; consult the NOFO for program-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and permanent residency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For CDA programs other than K99/R00, only U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or individuals lawfully admitted for permanent residence at the time an offer of an award is made are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals on temporary or student visas are not eligible unless they have begun the process for permanent residency and expect to be admitted by the earliest possible award date. Evidence of Permanent Resident Card (I-551) or other legal verification will be required prior to award; recipient institution is responsible for ensuring eligibility during award. K99/R00 has different citizenship-related rules detailed in its NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of appointment — full-time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time of award, all CDA recipients must have a full-time appointment at the applicant institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With prior NIH approval, awardees may hold part-time appointments for limited periods during the award (see Temporary Adjustments). Full-time or part-time is defined by institutional policy. Additional appointments (clinical practice, VA, etc.) cannot be used to meet the full-time appointment or effort requirement; dual appointees must still have a full-time appointment at the applicant institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary adjustments to full-time appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may request temporary reduction in appointment to less than full-time (but not less than three-quarter time) for up to 12 continuous months during the CDA project period under certain circumstances (e.g., parental leave, medical conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests will not be approved to accommodate job opportunities, clinical practice, clinical training, or joint appointments. Recipient must continue to commit at least 75% effort of the part-time appointment to research and career development. Recipient institution must submit a request and documentation to the awarding IC justifying the reduction, assuring continued institutional commitment, mentor must provide a revised mentoring plan with updated milestones, and institution must provide a revised statement of commitment to protected time. Salary and award costs will be reduced accordingly. Requests considered case-by-case; for transition CDAs (K22/K99) requests must address impact on ability to transition to R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of effort general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to full-time appointment, mentored and non-mentored CDA recipients must devote and maintain a minimum level of effort to the award; during a no-cost extension the recipient must maintain the effort minimum and can only reduce effort with prior IC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional appointments cannot be used to meet minimum effort. Contact IC program staff for questions about eligibility and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored CDA minimum effort (9 person months / 75%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored CDA recipients are required to devote a minimum commitment equivalent of 9 calendar person months (75% of full-time appointment) to the career development and research objectives specified in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remaining 3 person months (25%), if applicable, can be divided among other research, clinical, and teaching activities only if consistent with CDA goals (development into independent investigator). Some ICs allow less than 75% (not lower than 50%) effort for certain clinical specialties—consult the NOFO and IC staff for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related research and complementary effort policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored K recipients are encouraged to apply for additional research grants during their K award; complementary effort on other grants that include related research is allowed without salary support, but where there is scientific overlap the percent effort on the research grant is subsumed within the required CDA effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should not be significant duplication of the scope of research supported by the CDA. Related research must be consistent with the goals and objectives of the CDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent support reduction conditions (final two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided they remain in a mentored status, mentored CDA recipients in the final two years may reduce CDA effort to no less than 6 person months (50%) when they have competed successfully for peer-reviewed research awards (NIH or other Federal agency or non-Federal sources) of at least $100,000 in direct costs, and other agency policy allows it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are encouraged to obtain funding from NIH or other Federal sources as PD/PI on a competing research grant or as project leader on a competing multi-project award. Budgets for the competing research grant should request appropriate salary amounts; when the research grant is awarded, CDA effort may be reduced to 6 person months while maintaining total research commitment at 9 person months (75%) or more for the mentored CDA duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for salary support from competing research grant
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for salary support from peer-reviewed research awards from any Federal agency, the CDA recipient must be one of the named PD/PIs on a competing NIH research grant application (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34 or equivalent) or a sub-project director on a competing multi-component research or center grant/cooperative agreement (P01, P50, U01, etc.) and the CDA must be active and in its final two years at time of reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NIH submissions, a letter from the department chair or responsible institutional official must accompany the research grant application providing evidence that the recipient will continue to focus on career development, will continue access to their mentor, and that total research effort will be maintained (9 person months). For submissions to other Federal agencies, such a letter is strongly encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH adjustments when independent support obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: When mentored CDA recipients obtain independent support as described, the NIH awarding IC will adjust CDA effort to no less than 6 person months (50%) consistent with maintaining total research effort at 9 person months or 75% or more of full-time appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will adjust total salary support committed to the K award consistent with adjusted effort but will continue to provide full research development support costs (Other Personnel, Equipment, Travel, Participant/Trainee Support, Other Direct Costs). The K award may also be adjusted to avoid additional budget overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-mentored CDA effort expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators on independent (non-mentored) CDAs are generally required to devote a minimum of 3–6 person months (25–50% effort) to research and research career development activities during the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some independent CDAs require more than 6 person months (50%); for example, K02 recipients are required to devote 9 person months (75% effort). Independent recipients may receive additional salary support from other NIH/PHS grants for effort not committed to the CDA. Specific policies noted in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary adjustments to percent effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of award the candidate must meet applicable effort requirement, but recipients may request temporary reduction in effort for up to 12 continuous months during award for reasons such as parental leave, childcare, elder care, medical conditions, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For programs requiring 75% minimum, a recipient can request reduction to no less than 50%. Requests will not be approved to accommodate job opportunities, clinical practice, clinical training, or joint appointments. The recipient institution must submit documentation to the awarding IC justifying reduced effort and assuring continued institutional commitment; recipient must assure intention to return to 75% as soon as possible; mentor must provide revised mentoring plan and milestones. NIH will adjust total salary consistent with adjusted effort but will continue other research costs and the recipient may request an extension to account for reduced effort. Requests considered case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort reduction not available for some Independent CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: The temporary adjustment in effort policy is not available for Independent CDAs that require only 25–50% effort (e.g., K07 leadership, K05, and K24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients of these awards cannot use the temporary reduction option described for 75% effort programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous reduction in appointment status and percent effort
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not simultaneously request a reduction in appointment status from full-time to part-time AND a reduction in percent effort to less than 75%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mutually exclusive reductions per policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior research support eligibility (allowed prior awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: For most mentored CDAs, individuals are eligible to apply if they have previously served as PD/PI of R03, R21, R34/U34, R36, SBIR/STTR, Transition Scholar Award (K38) or been appointed to institutional career development programs (K12, KL2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The K99/R00 program has different prior support eligibility detailed in its NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior research support ineligibility (disqualifying prior awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, for mentored CDAs, individuals are NOT eligible if they are current or former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50), other major individual career development awards (e.g., DP5, K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K76, K99/R00), or Project Leads of P01/P50 sub-projects, or the equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most independent CDAs require the applicant have independent, peer-reviewed support at time of award; check NOFO for specifics and IC requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must contain Candidate Information, Statements of Support, Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate, and a Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidate information must justify the need for requested period of support and be tailored to prior research experience and career development needs; for mentored CDAs the plan must be designed to move the candidate from mentored to independent status. The Research Plan must have intrinsic research importance and serve as a vehicle for learning methodology, theories, and skills necessary for an independent researcher. For mentored awards, the research plan must include a description of the relationship between the mentor’s research and the candidate’s proposed research plan. Other than K22 from unaffiliated candidates, all applications require documents describing Environment and Institutional Commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment and environment documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant organization must define and document a strong, well-established research and career development program related to the candidate's area of interest and provide a statement of commitment to the candidate's development into an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution should describe facilities and resources, agreement to provide adequate time and support for proposed protected time for the entire award period, equipment, opportunities for intellectual interaction (courses, journal clubs, seminars), and a letter on institutional letterhead describing commitment. Institutional commitment may not be contingent upon receipt of the CDA. For off-site training, goals of total experience must be encompassed and supported under the appointment with applicant organization. Contact awarding IC for level of commitment required.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID identifier requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for ORCID identifiers will be enforced at the time of application for individual career development awards (K01, K02, K05, K07, K08, K18, K22, K23, K24, K25, K26, K38, K43, K76, and K99/R00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA system validations will check whether applicants have ORCID iDs and applications will not be accepted unless an ORCID iD is linked to the PD/PI's eRA Commons Personal Profile. Prospective applicants may link eRA profiles to existing ORCID accounts or create ORCID profiles via eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At least three (but no more than five) letters of reference are required for all new and resubmission mentored CDA applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be from individuals not directly involved in the application (mentors must not submit a separate letter) and may include advisory committee members. Letters should address the candidate's competence and potential to develop into an independent biomedical, behavioral, or clinical investigator. Reference letters are submitted directly by the referee through eRA Commons (not as part of Grants.gov application) and will be joined to the application in the eRA system. Missing required letters may delay review or lead to non-acceptance. See SF424(R&R) Application Guide for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent applications/duplicate submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not accept any application in response to an NOFO that is essentially the same as one currently pending initial review unless the applicant withdraws the pending application, nor will it accept an application that is essentially the same as one already reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not preclude submission of a substantial resubmission of an application already reviewed, but such resubmissions must include an Introduction addressing the previous critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR (Responsible Conduct of Research) instruction plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: All CDA applicants (mentored and non-mentored) must include a description of formal and informal activities related to instruction in the responsible conduct of research (RCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications lacking an RCR plan will be considered incomplete and may be delayed in review. Plans and past record will be rated as acceptable or unacceptable; unacceptable plans will not be funded until an acceptable revised plan is provided. The plan must address the five instructional components: format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency (detailed below). For additional information see the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion-based instruction in RCR is expected to include substantive face-to-face interaction among participants and faculty; video conferencing may be incorporated but should foster discussion, active learning, engagement and interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video conferencing should not be the sole means of instruction except in special short-term programs or well-justified unusual circumstances. Plans using only video conferencing will not be considered acceptable in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Subject matter topics
rubrics_metrics.description: While no specific curriculum is mandated, acceptable RCR plans generally include topics such as: (a) conflict of interest/commitment; (b) human subjects/live vertebrate animal policies and safe laboratory practices; (c) mentor/mentee responsibilities; (d) safe research environments free of discriminatory harassment; (e) collaborative research including industry and international collaborations; (f) peer review and confidentiality in peer review; (g) data acquisition and analysis, laboratory tools, recordkeeping practices; (h) secure and ethical data use, data confidentiality, management, sharing, ownership; (i) research misconduct and policies; (j) responsible authorship and publication; (k) scientist as responsible member of society, ethical issues, environmental and societal impacts of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses related to professional ethics or clinical research may be part of RCR training but are generally not sufficient alone to cover all aspects of responsible research conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Faculty participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors and other appropriate faculty are highly encouraged to contribute to both formal and informal RCR instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal instruction occurs through lab interactions year-round. For institutional Career Awards, training faculty may serve as discussion leaders, speakers, lecturers, or course directors. Rotating faculty can help achieve full faculty participation over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Duration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable RCR programs generally involve at least eight contact hours of substantive interaction among career recipients, mentors, and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semester-long series of seminars/programs may be more effective than single seminars or one-day workshops because topics can be considered in depth and learning consolidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR — Frequency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should be undertaken at least once during each career stage, and at a frequency of no less than once every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are encouraged to consider ongoing and discipline-specific training as individuals progress; advanced students/postdocs may benefit from more tailored, discipline-specific instruction.
